note: STC-2 live monitoring probe registry (post-audit Phase 2, 2026-08-21). Read by projects/status-center/monitor/bin/monitor.js. States are computed, never curated: LIVE / DEGRADED / DOWN / NOT_MONITORED. A probe that cannot run reports DOWN or NOT_MONITORED — never silent green.

probes.name: mythosprod.xyz (ecosystem hub)
probes.note: Apex deployed 2026-08-22: the Mythos Hub Dashboard is served from sites/mythosprod.xyz via /var/www/mythosprod.xyz, with TLS for mythosprod.xyz and www. BLOCKER-HUB-DNS is cleared. The probe is unchanged and still expects 200 — a DOWN here now means a real outage of the platform entry point, not a pending deployment.

probes.name: mythosprod.xyz/health.json (Hub dashboard endpoint)
probes.note: Distinct from hub-apex: hub-apex proves the site answers over HTTPS, this proves the dashboard's own health endpoint is served. Both must be green for the entry point to be whole.

probes.name: mythosprod.xyz/api/status.json (Hub status feed)
probes.note: The Hub reads its state through this same-origin alias onto this monitor's own output. The alias points outside the Hub's webroot, so it can break while the Hub itself still answers 200 — without this probe that failure is invisible. Probing our own output is not a loop: the result lands in the next snapshot.

probes.name: othmode.mythosprod.xyz (OTHMODE control platform)
probes.note: Same Node process as `ordre` on 127.0.0.1:3021 — two hostnames, one runtime. expect_content_type guards against an nginx catch-all answering for a dead upstream (the sya-api lesson).

probes.name: othmode.mythosprod.xyz Task Reports API (public read)
probes.note: This probe expected 401 until 7252de2 (2026-08-26) deliberately made the Task Reports a PUBLIC READ. The expectation was not updated with the release, so from 15:13Z the probe reported a false DOWN against a healthy service. 200 carrying a JSON body with "tasks" is the healthy state now: the route exists, is served by the current release, and answers with no credential. 404 remains the stale-process signature and still drives DOWN — expect_body_substring is set rather than status alone so that an empty or catch-all 200 cannot false-green (the sya-api lesson). This probe no longer asserts anything about authentication; that assertion moved to `othmode-authwall`, which is the only reason relaxing this one is safe.

probes.name: othmode.mythosprod.xyz authenticated API (auth wall)
probes.note: 401 IS the healthy state. This probe exists so that opening the read surface did not silently retire the auth-wall check `othmode-api` used to carry. /api/othmode/evolution/events genuinely still requires a session — it is the same endpoint tests/othmode-2-platform-test.js uses as its no-credential probe, so the monitor and the suite assert the same guarantee from opposite sides. A 200 here means an unauthenticated caller reached an administrative endpoint: a real security regression, and it must page. 404 means the running process is older than the evolution release. GET only — the monitor never issues a write; the separate guarantee that no POST route is public is asserted statically in the suite, never probed against production.

probes.name: SYA catalog API
probes.note: RETIRED — not pending. Verified on-host 2026-08-22: there is no SYA API to probe. The ssangyong.autos vhost is a static root with try_files and carries no /api proxy_pass, ssangyong-storefront.service is inactive, and /api/health, / and an invented nonsense path all return the byte-identical storefront index (md5 1d7337e470ed06d91c965cba40c7dad1). The catalog API is absent, not merely unhealthy, so NOT_MONITORED is the accurate state for a system that no longer exists. Keep expect_content_type alongside the disabled flag: if the API is ever restored, flipping enabled is then sufficient, and the content-type assertion is what stops the SPA fallback from reporting a dead API as LIVE. Re-enable only when a real JSON endpoint exists.

probes.name: idauto-postgres (database)
probes.note: ENABLED 2026-08-22: the precondition this note asked for is met — idauto-postgres publishes 127.0.0.1:5432 (docker ps: 127.0.0.1:5432->5432/tcp; ss -ltn confirms LISTEN), so the port is host-reachable without docker group membership and deploy's exclusion from that group is untouched. This is a TCP connect only: it opens a socket, observes that the server accepts it, and closes. It sends no startup packet, authenticates nothing, reads no business data, writes nothing, and needs no credential. Postgres logs the closed connection as a reset, which is expected for a liveness check. Loopback-only, so it also proves the port is not publicly exposed. The handshake is why this is not merely a port check: the port is published through docker-proxy, which accepts the client BEFORE it dials the container, so a bare TCP connect would report LIVE against a wedged or absent PostgreSQL. Sending the 8-byte SSLRequest and requiring the protocol's own 'S'/'N' reply closes that false green. It still proves the server speaks PostgreSQL and is accepting connections, not that any particular database or query works — the backup job remains the end-to-end proof.

probes.name: Off-host backup system
probes.note: Reads the health record written by ops/backup/mythos-backup-run.sh. A missing record is DOWN, never unknown-green.
